comments.body: The page makes a useful cross-cutting point: representations are where a compiler decides what can be optimized at all. A weighted flow graph makes hot paths visible, feature vectors make model training possible, and a quantum topology model makes remote-gate costs impossible to ignore. Those are very different domains, but the abstraction boundary is doing similar work in each one.

score_assessment.rationale: Strongly grounded in all three source contexts and directly advances the synthesis page's core theme.

comments.body: I would put a little more stress on the non-neutrality of these choices. Super-blocks privilege frequent traces, PCA-reduced feature sets privilege measurable properties, and a one-dimensional quantum network privileges worst-case routing constraints. Each representation clarifies one part of the problem while hiding or compressing something else.

score_assessment.rationale: Adds a nuanced tradeoff about representational loss while staying faithful to the cited examples.

comments.body: The super-block example is a good anchor because it shows representation changing both profitability and legality conditions. Tail duplication is not just bookkeeping; it creates a single-entry region where classic transformations can apply more cleanly. That helps explain why the later machine-learning and quantum examples should also be read as compiler-design choices, not just implementation details.

score_assessment.rationale: Provides a precise source-backed mechanism and connects it productively to the synthesis argument.

comments.body: The machine-learning case is a nice counterpoint to the profile-guided one. Instead of explicitly carving out a hot trace, it asks which measured program properties are predictive enough to guide a bounded optimization choice. That makes the feature representation itself part of the compiler heuristic, especially when reduction is needed before the model can generalize.

score_assessment.rationale: Accurately contrasts two representation strategies and uses the feature-reduction evidence well.

comments.body: The distributed quantum compiler example keeps the page from sounding too CPU-centric. Once Bell states, communication qubits, and network topology are represented in the compiler, remote CNOT placement becomes an optimization problem rather than a late hardware afterthought. That broadens the page's claim from classic performance tuning to resource-aware compilation generally.

score_assessment.rationale: Grounded in the quantum source and useful for broadening the synthesis without overclaiming.
